data.description:
SOURCE: board comment on AS-93 from the Lattice dashboard (actor dashboard:web, 2026-09-10T15:30Z): "keep in mind for this the lattice port is not fixed". Filed by the CTO as the option NOT taken in the AS-93 ruling (see that ruling comment), so the alternative is on the record rather than lost.

STATUS OF THIS TASK IS CONTINGENT. It exists because the board's comment has two readings and I asked him which he meant (DM conversation 7, this tick). If he confirms he wants the dashboard port to be movable, this task activates and becomes critical Chat-set work. If he confirms 8799 is fine and the comment meant "do not assume it is running / do not assume it forever", this task is CANCELLED, not built. Do not pull it into planning before that answer lands.

THE PROBLEM, STATED CORRECTLY. The dashboard port is not one value in one place. It is a three-legged coupling and no leg alone is authoritative:
  L1  the port `lattice dashboard` binds. CLI flag `--port`, default 8799 (verified: lattice/cli/dashboard_cmd.py:49; `lattice restart` defaults to the same at :143). Today supplied by hand in a live session; after AS-94 it is declared by the launchd plist.
  L2  the Tailscale serve mapping that publishes it on the tailnet. Verified live: `https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net:8443 -> http://127.0.0.1:8799`. This state lives in tailscaled, NOT in this repo, and chat cannot read it.
  L3  the two constants in apps/chat/public/dashboard-link.js: LOOPBACK_PORT=8799, REMOTE_PORT=8443.
Move L1 without L2 and the phone breaks. Move L1 and L2 without L3 and both break. LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL does not solve it: it is a single verbatim base, so it can express "this one URL everywhere" but never "port X on loopback, port Y over the tailnet" — setting it to a loopback URL with a new port fixes the Mac and re-breaks the phone.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST "ADD A CONFIG KEY". The obvious move — have the server publish `latticeDashboardPort` over the /api/config channel AS-93 already builds, and let the client compose `:port` locally — removes the hard-coding in L3 only. The tailnet link stays correct only if L2 moved too, and nothing in the repo can observe L2. That is a knob that reads as a fix and is not one. So the scope here is the coupling, not the constant:
  - ONE declared value that L1 and L3 both read (candidate: an env value consumed by the launchd plist render and published to the browser via /api/config, with the client deriving `:port` for a loopback page and keeping the tailnet port from the same declaration).
  - L2 handled honestly: either it becomes a repo artifact with a render/verify recipe (AS-94 currently lists that as OUT of scope — revisit here, do not silently import it), or it stays host state and the docs name it as the one leg that must be moved by hand, in the same procedure, with the check that proves it moved.
  - Precedence with LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL settled in writing BEFORE any code: a verbatim base override and a port declaration can contradict each other, and AS-93's rule 1 (override wins verbatim) must either survive or be deliberately replaced. An unstated precedence rule is how this comes back a third time.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST BE REUSED, NOT REBUILT (this is why merging AS-93 first costs nothing):
  - apps/chat/public/dashboard-link.js is a pure module and the SINGLE point of change — the two ports are exported constants and AS-93's AC-9 bans 8799/8443/127.0.0.1 literals anywhere else in public/, enforced by a test that enumerates the directory. There is no second place to fix.
  - GET /api/config exists, with an explicit allowlist and an exact-key-set assertion in test/api.test.js standing guard over it. A new key is an additive change to a guarded channel.
  - AS-94's plist template is where L1 gets declared, and its AC-2 already asserts the rendered ProgramArguments.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA are deliberately NOT written yet: they depend on which reading the board confirms, and writing them now would anchor the eventual plan on a design chosen before the requirement was known. The planner writes them, and per M4 each stated property names its own falsifier — including at least one that observes a link go WRONG when one of the three legs is moved alone, since "the legs are coupled" is the entire claim this task makes.

RELATION: AS-93 (client helper and the two constants) and AS-94 (the launchd job that declares L1). Neither depends_on this; this depends on both being merged, because it edits what they build.
data.title: Chat tooling: make the Lattice dashboard port one declared value across the launchd job, the tailnet mapping, and the client helper (CONTINGENT on the board's answer)

data.body:
CTO disposition, 2026-09-10 (tick watcher:17217:26a2eb602b99ba56), from board DM msg 632: 'I am going to work on lattice port stuff upstream on the lattice project itself.'

DECISION: CANCELLED. Not parked.

Reasoning. This task was filed contingent on one of two readings of the board's 'the lattice port is not fixed' comment: (a) the port is a movable flag, so the three-legged coupling (L1 launchd plist, L2 Tailscale serve mapping, L3 dashboard-link.js constants) needs one declared value in this repo; or (b) the comment meant 'do not assume something is listening', which AS-94 already answers. Msg 632 is a third answer neither reading anticipated: the port question moves OUT of this repo and into upstream Lattice, which the board maintains. Whatever upstream does — a declared/discoverable port, a config file in .lattice/, a fixed default, removing --port — it changes the shape of L1 and therefore what L3 should read. Designing an in-repo coupling now would be building against a target the board is about to move; the precedence rule with LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL, the L2 handling, and the acceptance criteria would all be written for a Lattice that will not exist by the time this task reached planning.

Why cancel rather than leave it in backlog at low priority: AS-95's continue-predicate rule (b) counts any backlog task whose depends_on targets are done as READY. Both of this task's depends_on (AS-93 done; AS-94 next) will be satisfied soon, so a 'parked' AS-96 would be picked up by the loop as real work the moment AS-94 merges — a parked task with met dependencies is not parked in a loop-driven company. Cancellation keeps the record (the coupling analysis in the description is still correct and is the reference for whoever touches this next) without making it schedulable.

What stands unchanged: AS-94 declares --port 8799 in the plist (its AC-2); dashboard-link.js keeps LOOPBACK_PORT=8799 / REMOTE_PORT=8443 with AS-93's AC-9 literal ban; LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL wins verbatim (AS-93 rule 1).

WHAT RE-OPENS THIS (as a NEW task referencing this description — do not resurrect this one, its acceptance criteria were never written and its premise has changed):
  1. Upstream Lattice changes the dashboard default port, or removes/renames --port. Impact: AS-94's plist ProgramArguments and AC-2 guard, dashboard-link.js LOOPBACK_PORT, and the Tailscale serve mapping (host state, hand-moved) all need to move together — file it as a single Chat-set task with the three legs enumerated, and per M4 name the falsifier that observes a link go WRONG when one leg moves alone.
  2. Upstream Lattice ships a port DECLARATION this repo can read (e.g. in .lattice/ config or a dashboard-reported value). Then L1 and L3 read that declaration instead of a repo constant: a new task to consume it, additive to /api/config (exact-key-set guard in test/api.test.js must be updated in the same change) and to the plist render recipe. L2 remains host state either way unless the board decides otherwise.
  3. The board says in writing that the port should be movable from THIS repo after all. Then reading (a) is confirmed and the description here is the spec.

Not in this repo's scope from here: anything about the dashboard port that lives in the Lattice project. If a tick notices a port-related upstream change (lattice --version bump with a different default, a dashboard that refuses --port), it reports it and files per item 1 or 2; it does not improvise a fix in dashboard-link.js.
